speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I see you have a pruritic rash along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any specific pattern to the rash, such as it starting on your trunk and spreading?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal CBC and liver results. Given your recent exposure to cold air and your symptoms of rhinorrhea and headache, have you noticed any wheezing or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that clarification. Based on the facial rash sparing the perioral area and the preceding viral symptoms, have you or your family noticed any joint pain or swelling, and has anyone else at home developed similar symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear_Antibody (ANA)
REQUEST TEST: Rheumatoid_Factor

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those negative autoimmune results. Given the facial rash sparing the mouth and the preceding viral illness, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of a specific viral exanthem; could you describe the shape of the rash, such as whether it presents as red cheeks with a pale area around the mouth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.
